text:
ops-bot: Release train notice — brief pause for staged rollouts to resolve a canary flake seen in eu-west-1. Please read instructions below. :pause_button:

sam: TL;DR: we're pausing non-urgent canaries in eu-west-1 for 3 hours to investigate a flake in our batching layer that surfaced at ~09:04 UTC. If you have a critical security or data-loss fix, follow the emergency flow.

rukmini: Adding detail: the flake looks like intermittent 502s from the runtime when payloads exceed 4k tokens under specific batching conditions. We've reproduced locally with the stress harness. No signed-off production regressions yet but we want to be cautious.

chris: Question — does this affect embeddings pipelines or only text generation?

rukmini: Affects text-gen paths where continuous batching + prefix-cache was enabled. Embeddings and lightweight rerank unaffected. We'll set a temporary feature-toggle to disable aggressive batching for affected models.

pager: Incident/ops note: No SLA breaches yet. We've routed non-critical traffic to fallback variant in us-east-1 and raised a paging alert if error rate >1% sustained for 3m. Dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rollouts/eu-batch-flake

sam: Emergency flow reminder: label PR `critical-hotfix` or `security-hotfix`, include the smoke commands, and DM @oncall. Use the CLI: `rw release start --canary-tag emergency --window 20m --regions eu-west-1 --approvers oncall,sam` and add `--note "batching-flake"`.

chris: If we need to abort a canary quickly, what's the fastest sequence?

pager: Fast abort: `rw release abort --id <release-id>` then `kubectl rollout pause deployment/<svc> -n production`. If traffic still spikes, run `kubectl annotate svc <svc> redwood/force-fallback=true -n infra` to trigger fallback routing.

rukmini: I'll push a hotfix branch that disables the aggressive batching optimization and run the harness. Expect a test PR in ~25m.

oncall: I'll standby for the PR. Remember to include the smoke script output in the PR description. I'll approve urgent ones inline.

sam: Devex note: updating the release train docs with the temporary rule — no non-critical canaries in eu-west-1 until the hold is lifted. Adding a short FAQ on what qualifies as critical.

chris: Ops ask — can we add a health check that measures token-length distribution to catch this earlier?

rukmini: Yes, adding that to follow-ups. We'll also create a regression test in the eval harness for >4k token payloads.

ops-bot: Next update in 30 minutes or on any change. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
